question: Which questions should a coordinator answer before adding a new agent to an agent team, so that duplicate or one-off agents are not created?
method: Read the captured role core of an internal team-design agent at a pinned commit, and checked that the same seven questions appear unchanged in the two earlier revisions of that role recorded in its lock. Restated the questions in new words; no role text was copied. No web search or provider calls were used.
queries: necessity questions applied before adding an agent role
decision rule when a necessity question fails
findings: The role applied seven necessity questions before any other design check: recurring work, own judgment, own knowledge, a named work product, no existing owner, measurable quality, and a condition for retiring or changing the role.
A failed question meant no new role or an open decision for a person.
Implementation checks (owner, bounded inputs and outputs, least tools, handoff placement, evaluation and escalation, dependencies) came after necessity and did not replace it.
The role's newer upstream revision replaced the explicit questions with a registry match; the questions themselves were stable in the earlier revisions.
adopted: The seven questions as a standalone check any coordinator can load before adding an agent.
All seven yes to add; any no means do not add and route the work elsewhere; otherwise an open decision with a named decider.
Evidence per answer, and the closest existing agent named every time.
rejected: Designing the whole team, writing role contracts, or building the agent inside this skill; those are separate jobs with their own authority.
skipped: Interview scripts, document templates, and course or classroom material from the source role.

sources.title: Captured role core of the fleet team-design agent
findings: The method section lists the seven necessity questions and says a failed test means no hire or an open decision.
Implementation checks follow necessity and do not replace it.
